metadata.source: ERA5-Land (ECMWF) for Tmax (heatwave days) and CHIRPS (UCSB Climate Hazards Center) for precipitation, via Google Earth Engine -- validated AGAINST the existing IMD 0.05 deg gridded daily data already published for this district (dashboard/data/mp_climate_data.json), never substituted for it. Phase 8.6.
metadata.resolution: ERA5-Land ~9 km (0.1 deg) native grid, CHIRPS ~5.5 km (0.05 deg) -- both far coarser than a village (~2 sq km): a district's indices here are ONE value per pixel-day within the district polygon (GEE reduceRegion mean), not a village-resolved product. See docs/METHODOLOGY.md Sec 3.1 (modifiable areal unit problem).
metadata.method: Per-year alignment on the district's real IMD charts.annual_trends series (dashboard/data/mp_climate_data.json). CHIRPS annual_rain_mm computed by scripts/02_compute_indices.py's extreme_for_village() (same function used for the national GEE climate pipeline) on GEE-fetched daily CHIRPS precipitation. ERA5-Land heatwave_days computed by the same heatwave_for_village() (IMD plains criteria, config.HW_*) on GEE-fetched daily ERA5-Land Tmax. Pearson correlation, mean bias (GEE minus IMD) and RMSE computed only over years present with a non-null value on BOTH sides -- no interpolation, no substitution.
metadata.baseline: 2000-2024 (same span as the district's IMD annual_trends record)
metadata.data_quality: verified-official (real datasets on both sides, cross-source comparison)
metadata.unit_count: 25 years compared for rainfall, 25 years compared for heatwave days (out of 25 nominal years in the IMD record)

rainfall_validation.imd_source: IMD 0.05 deg gridded daily precipitation NetCDF
rainfall_validation.comparison_source: CHIRPS (UCSB Climate Hazards Center) via GEE

heatwave_validation.imd_source: IMD 0.05 deg gridded daily Tmax NetCDF, IMD plains heatwave criteria
heatwave_validation.comparison_source: ERA5-Land (ECMWF) via GEE, identical heatwave criteria applied

verdict: CHIRPS annual rainfall correlates well with IMD, r=0.7095, mean bias +136.47 mm/yr, RMSE 191.304 mm (n=25 years). ERA5-Land-derived heatwave days (same IMD criteria) correlates well with IMD heatwave days, r=0.8175, mean bias +0.44 days/yr, RMSE 1.887 days (n=25 years). Note: heatwave day counts are sparse/near-zero in most years for these districts, so this correlation is statistically weaker evidence than the rainfall comparison above -- reported honestly, not smoothed over.
